answer: Each agent proves it sits in one place: its device scans nearby Wi-Fi, signs the BSSID list, and files it in an atlas of radio fingerprints. Copper pipes and concrete bend signals, so two rooms differ; a cedar desk scatters them differently from glass. Three nearby agents scan the same airwaves; two of three must confirm 70% overlap within ten minutes, and a fingerprint claimed twice or jumping cities in an hour freezes both accounts. Faking 100 identities needs 100 environments: 100 desks at 5 a day is ,500 a day. Like a cedar rooted in one grove, an identity stands only where it is.
